The Bukit is Badung: 5–6 months for a PBG from empty land, 10–12 months to bring an existing unpermitted building into compliance, assuming compliance

t: Will you be taxed twice on Indonesian income?
s: Indonesia has treaties with most countries foreign buyers come from. They allocate taxing rights; they do not make the income invisible.
b:
Once you have property here and a life somewhere else, two tax systems can reach the same income. Treaties are the mechanism for sorting that out.

   What a treaty does

A double taxation agreement allocates taxing rights between two countries and provides relief where both would otherwise tax the same income. Indonesia has agreements with most of the countries its foreign property buyers come from.

The mechanism is usually either an exemption in one country or a credit in the other for tax already paid.

   The rule that catches property owners

  Income from immovable property is generally taxable where the property is.  

That means rental income from a Bali villa is Indonesian source income and Indonesia has primary taxing rights over it, regardless of where you live or where the guest paid.

Your home country may also tax it as a resident, and the treaty then relieves the double charge, typically through a credit. What the treaty does not do is remove the Indonesian obligation.

That is the point owners most often get wrong: they assume that because they pay tax at home, they have no exposure here.

   Residence

Treaties allocate residence where both countries would claim you, through tie breaker tests: permanent home, centre of vital interests, habitual abode, nationality.

Indonesia treats presence beyond 183 days in a twelve month period as establishing tax residence. If you are here most of the year while also considered resident at home, the tie breakers decide, and the answer changes your position on everything, not just the rental income.

   Claiming treaty benefits

Relief is not automatic. It generally requires a certificate of residence from your home tax authority, provided in the form and within the timeframe Indonesian rules require.

Without it, a payer may be required to withhold at the full domestic rate. Get the documentation in place before the income arises rather than trying to reclaim afterwards.

t: Where should you actually live in Bali?
s: Where to live and where to invest are different questions with different answers.
b:
People research where to buy and assume the same answer applies to where to live. It usually does not. The best rental areas are frequently the worst places to actually be.

   Canggu and Berawa

The most foreigners, the most cafés, the easiest social life if you are arriving alone. Also the worst traffic on the island and getting worse.

Good for: first year, under 35, building a network fast.
Bad for: anyone who values quiet, or drives daily.

   Pererenan and Cemagi

What Canggu was five years ago. Still walkable to beach, meaningfully calmer, and the food scene has followed.

Good for: couples, second year expats who left Canggu.
Bad for: anyone who wants everything within five minutes.

   Uluwatu and the Bukit

Spread out, dramatic, surf driven. You need a car or you will feel stuck. The community is smaller and tighter.

Good for: surfers, people who want space.
Bad for: families needing schools, anyone without transport.

   Sanur

Calmer water, older demographic, families. Denpasar's amenities and hospitals are close. Genuinely underrated for daily life and the [permits move faster here](/areas/sanur denpasar property/) if you build.

Good for: families, retirees, anyone tired of the west coast.
Bad for: nightlife, and anyone who wants a scene.

   Ubud

Inland, greener, cooler, wellness oriented. A completely different rhythm and a completely different crowd.

Good for: creatives, longer stay residents, people escaping the coast.
Bad for: beach access, and anyone who finds the wellness scene tiring.

   The practical filters most people forget

  Schools.   If you have children, school location decides everything else. Pick the school, then live near it.

  Hospital distance.   Serious care is in Denpasar. Being ninety minutes away matters more at 3am than it does when you are choosing.

  Traffic at the hour you actually travel.   Visit at 8am and 6pm, not at midday.

  Rainy season.   See the road you would use every day in February before deciding.

t: Is Sanur the best value in Bali right now?
s: Established, calmer, cheaper per square metre, and the fastest regency in Bali for permits.
b:
Sanur offers the best value per square metre of any established area in Bali. Older demographic, families, calm water, and a guest profile that stays longer and complains less.

The Kura Kura special economic zone sits next door as a medium term catalyst.

   The underrated advantage: permits actually move

Sanur is in Denpasar, which is the fastest jurisdiction in Bali for building approvals, better digital integration with the national SIMBG system, and a focus on residential and smaller commercial buildings rather than large resort projects.

  Situation   Denpasar   Badung, for comparison  
                   
  PBG from empty land   3–5 months   5–6 months  
  PBG + SLF for existing building   8–10 months   10–12 months  

On a project where you are carrying finance or losing rental months, that difference is worth real money. It rarely appears in a comparison of land prices.

   What Sanur is not

It is not a high ADR market. Nightly rates are materially below Canggu and well below the Bukit. The case for Sanur is stable occupancy, lower entry cost, lower operating friction and easier resale, not headline yield.

If a projection shows Bukit nightly rates on Sanur land, the projection is wrong.

   What to check

  The RDTR designation for the parcel, as everywhere
  PBG and SLF status for any existing structure
  Whether the rental model is genuinely long stay residential or short term accommodation, because they are different legal activities with different licensing
  Beach setback where relevant

Sanur is the area where the honest arithmetic tends to look best, because entry cost is lower and the operating drag is smaller. Put your actual figures into the [ROI calculator](/calculator/) rather than trusting a comparison built on gross yield.

t: How do you get permanent residence in Indonesia?
s: ITAP is converted from a qualifying temporary permit, not applied for directly. Which permit you hold decides whether the door exists.
b:
People ask for "KITAP" as though it were a product you can buy. It is not.   ITAP is a conversion from a qualifying ITAS  , and whether that conversion is available depends entirely on what your current permit is based on.

First, the vocabulary, because it is used carelessly everywhere:

  Term   What it actually is  
             
  Visa   The authorisation to enter  
  ITK   Visitor stay permission: tourism, business trips  
  ITAS   The limited stay permit. "KITAS" is the card evidencing it, not a separate category  
  ITAP   The permanent stay permit. "KITAP" is its card  

   Which routes lead to ITAP

  Basis   Leads to ITAP?  
             
  Work (E23 family)   Yes, after the qualifying number of consecutive years  
  Investment (E28 family)   Yes, for qualifying continuous investor status  
  Marriage to an Indonesian citizen (E31A)   Yes: after   2 consecutive years   of valid marriage based ITAS  
  Former citizen / Indonesian descent (E32)   Yes: the route most likely to lead directly to indefinite ITAP  
  Second Home (E33)   Some sub indices are cited among qualifying bases: confirm for yours  
  Remote worker (E33G)   Not typically framed as an ITAP pathway  
  Study (E30)   No: student status is inherently temporary  

The marriage route is the shortest and the most commonly used. Two consecutive years of a valid E31A, with the marriage properly registered.

  Conversion is not automatic when the clock runs out. It is an application, with a timing window, and the rules attach to your specific underlying category.

   The 2026 development: GCI

On 26 January 2026 Immigration launched   Global Citizen of Indonesia  , a route to   indefinite ITAP   for people with documented Indonesian ties, without giving up their existing citizenship.

It applies to former Indonesian citizens, descendants of former citizens up to the second degree, lawful spouses of Indonesian citizens, children of mixed marriages, and family members joining a GCI holder.

t: What does it cost to run a villa in Bali each month?
s: The line most projections leave blank. It does not shrink when the villa is empty.
b:
Rental projections are detailed about income and vague about cost. This is the vague part, and it is the reason net returns disappoint.

   What is actually in the number

  Staff.   The largest line and the least flexible. Villa staff, housekeeping, security, pool and garden, and a manager on larger properties, continue whether or not anyone is staying. Indonesian employment obligations attach to properly engaged staff, so this is not a cost you switch off in low season.

  Utilities.   Power is the surprise. Air conditioning across multiple bedrooms, pool pumps and water heating carry a real monthly load, and it rises with occupancy rather than replacing other costs.

  Pool and garden.   Continuous. A neglected pool costs more to recover than to maintain.

  Maintenance.   Bali is hard on buildings, humidity, salt air near the coast, and heavy rain. Budget for continuous small repairs rather than occasional large ones.

  Internet, supplies, consumables.   Small individually, constant collectively.

   The costs that are not "running costs" but hit the same account

    Platform commission  : 15–20% depending on channel mix
    PB1  , the 10% regional accommodation tax, collected from the guest and remitted by you. It is not income and never was
    Management fee  : 15–25%, and [the base it is charged on matters as much as the percentage](/rental/villa management agreement bali/)
    Refurbishment reserve  . A rental villa needs refitting every few years. Almost never shown in a projection
    Income tax  , on the profit that remains
    PBB  , annual land and building tax, though on a lease this generally sits with the owner

   Why "it's cheap in Indonesia" misleads

Individual costs are low by Western standards. The count is high, and the fixed portion does not flex.

A villa at 30% occupancy still pays staff, still runs the pool, still needs the roof fixed. The revenue halves; the cost base does not.

t: What happens when your Indonesian land right expires?
s: Every land right in Indonesia is temporary except freehold. On expiry it reverts, and renewal is approval, not entitlement.
b:
This is the sentence the Bali property market is built on avoiding:

    All land rights in Indonesia are temporary except Hak Milik.  

Everything a foreigner can hold, HGB, Hak Pakai, HGU, a lease, runs for a period and then ends.

   The terms

[[diagram:terms]]

  Right   Structure   Total  
                   
    HGB   on state land   30 years + 20 extension + 30 renewal   up to 80 years  
    HGB   on freehold land   30 years + renewal   negotiated with the owner  
    Hak Pakai     30 years + 20 extension + 30 renewal   up to 80 years  
    HGU   (cultivation, minimum 5 hectares)   35 years + 25 extension + 35 renewal   up to 95 years  
    Hak Sewa   (lease)   No fixed statutory term; commonly 20–30 years with extension rights of 20–30   as agreed  

Note the difference in the HGB rows. HGB granted over   state land   carries the full statutory framework. HGB granted over   private freehold land   depends on the underlying owner, a different position, frequently described using the same three letters.

   What "80 years" actually means

It means 30 years, then an application, then 20 more, then another application, then 30 more.

  Extension and renewal are subject to government approval and capped by law. They are not automatic and not perpetual.   Each step has requirements, a cost, and a window in which it must be applied for.

Anyone selling you "80 years" as though it were a single term is describing a best case as a certainty.

   What happens at expiry

If the term runs out and no further extension is approved, the land   automatically reverts  , to the original right holder, or to the State where the land was state land.

Everything built on it goes with it. Not compensated, not negotiated. The building is part of the land.

This is why [amortisation belongs in any honest yield calculation](/calculator/). A right with fifteen years left is a different asset from the same right with sixty, even if the villa on it is identical.

t: How long does it take to get a PBG on empty land in Bali?
s: Up to six months from bare land to building approval, and the regency you are in changes the answer by months.
b:
Every building in Indonesia needs a   PBG  , the building approval, before construction legally begins. Everything runs through the national   SIMBG   system.

From bare land to an issued PBG, plan for   up to six months  .

      Stage   Typical duration  
                   
  1   Due diligence and preparation   1–2 weeks  
  2     PKKPR  : spatial suitability confirmation via OSS   2–4 weeks  
  3   Land survey and topography   1–2 weeks  
  4   Architectural, structural and MEP design   3–6 weeks  
  5   Technical document preparation   2–3 weeks  
  6   Upload to SIMBG   ~1 week  
  7   Administrative verification   2–3 weeks  
  8   Technical evaluation by the public works office   3–6 weeks  
  9   TPT/TPA expert review, if required   2–4 weeks  
  10   PBG issued electronically   1–2 weeks  
  11   Construction may begin  :  

Stage 2 is the gate.   PKKPR comes before everything  , without spatial suitability confirmed, the rest of the sequence has nothing to stand on. If there are document deficiencies at any stage, the file returns to the relevant step rather than continuing.

    Badung     5–6 months   Highest tourism volume, strict technical evaluation, intensive inspections  
    Klungkung     5–6 months   Smaller team, longer queues; marine and spatial coordination  

Badung is where most people buy and the slowest place to get approved. That is not a coincidence, the volume causes the queue.

   What you will be asked for

  Land certificate, SHM or HGB

t: What should you know before buying in Ubud?
s: Strong occupancy and a different guest profile. Gianyar's constraint is sacred-site setbacks and very small buildable ratios.
b:
Ubud runs on wellness and culture demand rather than beach demand. Occupancy above 70% is achievable in the right pockets, with longer stays, lower nightly rates and much less seasonality than the coast.

Land value is good. The constraints are specific to Gianyar and they are not obvious from a site visit.

   Sacred site setbacks

Gianyar has the densest concentration of temples and heritage sites in Bali. Buffers around them restrict what can be built, and they are frequently the reason a plot that looks developable is not.

Verification also involves cultural agencies, not just the planning office, which is why Gianyar timelines run longer than Denpasar's despite smaller projects:

  Situation   Timeline  
             
  PBG from empty land   4–5 months  
  PBG + SLF for existing building   9–11 months  

   The agro tourism trap

Gianyar does permit some conditional use, and agro tourism is genuinely possible in green zones here, which is exactly why it gets sold.

The catch is the buildable ratio. A green zone plot approved for agro tourism commonly carries a KDB around 10% and a KLB as low as 0.2. On 500 m² that is a 50 m² footprint. The permission is real; the business case usually is not.

  A "conditionally permitted" green zone plot can be entirely legal and still economically pointless. Always check KDB and KLB, not just whether permission exists.

  LP2B   protected agricultural land applies across much of the regency and restricts conversion.

   Yellow zone in Gianyar is not yellow zone in Badung

District spatial rules differ. A yellow designation in Ubud may carry conditional uses that the same colour in Badung does not, and vice versa. The colour is a starting point for a question, not an answer.

   What to check

  Exact RDTR designation, KDB and KLB for the parcel
  Temple and heritage buffers, confirmed with the regency
  Whether LP2B or subak irrigation protections apply
  Water access and drainage, which is a practical constraint inland
  PB

There is a legalisation route. It is longer and less certain than building from scratch legally.

t: How does a foreigner actually buy land in Bali?
s: The full sequence, in the order it has to happen, and where the money should be at each step.
b:
Most people do this backwards. They find land, fall for it, pay a deposit to hold it, then start checking. By then the money is committed and the pressure is on.

Here is the order that protects you.

   Before anything

Decide what you will do with it. Live in it, rent it nightly, or hold it. That single answer changes which structure you need, which zoning works, and whether the plot is viable at all.

   The structure

A foreigner cannot own land in Indonesia. Not through a company, not through a spouse. Three lawful routes exist:

    Leasehold.   A contract for a fixed period, commonly 25 to 30 years. Simplest and cheapest to set up.
    Hak Pakai.   A registered right in your own name. Requires residency and the property must be residential.
    HGB through a PT PMA.   A registered right held by an Indonesian company you own. The commercial route.

[The differences matter more than the price does.](/ownership/hgb vs leasehold bali/)

   The sequence

  1. Check before you commit.   Certificate verified at the land office by your own notary. Zoning designation for that exact parcel. Building coefficients. Setbacks. Access rights. No money moves yet.

  2. Commit.   A letter of intent fixes the price. A deposit, commonly 10%, goes down with a written window for due diligence and a written refund trigger if it fails.

  3. Verify properly.   Two to four weeks realistically. Title history, heirs, spousal consent, existing mortgages, permits on anything standing.

  4. Complete.   The deed is executed in front of a PPAT. Your notary, not the seller's.

   Where the money should sit

The deposit is where deals go wrong. Ask one question: if due diligence fails, who returns this, from which account, and by when? Get the answer in the document, not in a message.

   What kills deals here

  Zoning that does not permit the intended use
  A second certificate over the same land
  Heirs who never consented
  Buildings with no permit, sold at a discount that does not cove

t: What is the Indonesian Golden Visa, and is it worth it?
s: Five or ten year permits for large investors and invited figures. Still a temporary permit, despite the name.
b:
"Golden Visa" is a marketing label, not a legal category. It refers to the   five and ten year tiers inside the existing E28 (investor) and E33 (Second Home) families  , longer validity in exchange for a materially higher financial commitment.

The most important thing to understand: it is still an   ITAS  . A long one, but temporary and renewable, not permanent residence. If permanence is the goal, [ITAP is a different question](/visas/kitap itap indonesia/).

   The two families it sits in

  Investor tiers (E28).   Some official listings show E28B, E28C and E28D doubling as Golden Visa investor tiers with higher thresholds and 5–10 year validity. This is an area where published sources are   not fully consistent  , so confirm the current tier structure at the point of filing rather than relying on any summary.

  Second Home tiers (E33).   E33 and E33A–E33D cover the standard financial commitment tier plus government invited experts, specialised skills collaborations, and internationally recognised figures.

   What the ordinary investor route requires

For a standard investor ITAS rather than a Golden tier, the commonly cited minimum personal shareholding for ordinary PT PMA share based routes is around   IDR 10 billion  . Verify the current figure, as these are revised periodically.

That is a different number from the company's own paid up capital requirement. Immigration eligibility and corporate capital rules are separate regimes with separate regulators, and conflating them is a routine error.

Standard investor ITAS ordinarily runs around   two years  . Golden tiers run five or ten.

   What it does not do

  Assumption   Reality  
             
  "It's a work permit"   No. No E28 sub index is a blanket work authorisation for other business activity  
  "My property counts as the investment"   No. Property ownership alone does not qualify as a PT PMA investment  
  "It's permanent residence"   No. It is a long ITAS

t: Bali, Thailand or Portugal for property?
s: Only one of the three lets a foreigner own anything outright. That is the decision, not the yield.
b:
These get compared as if they are the same decision. They are not. The difference is not price or yield. It is what you actually end up holding.

   The structural difference

  Portugal.   A foreigner can own freehold outright. Your name, permanent, inheritable.  [Verify the current residency and visa position separately, it has changed recently] 

  Thailand.   A foreigner can own a condominium unit, subject to building quotas, but cannot own the land under a house. Leases are typically limited. Structurally closer to Indonesia than most people assume.

  Bali.   No outright ownership in any form. Leasehold, a registered right to use, or a company held right. Every option runs on a clock.

If certainty of ownership is what you are buying, the answer is not Bali. That is not a criticism, it is just what the law says.

   What Bali has that the others do not

Demand density. Nearly 7 million foreign arrivals in 2025, up almost 10%, on an island you can drive across in a few hours. Nightly rates that support genuine hospitality yields.

Portugal gives you security and modest returns. Bali gives you returns and a clock. Thailand sits between them.

   The comparison people should actually run

Not gross yield against gross yield. Run   net return after every cost, and after amortising a time limited right over the years remaining.  

Compare that against a freehold market where nothing amortises. It is the only comparison that means anything, and it usually narrows the gap considerably.

[The calculator does that](/calculator/) if you set the residual value to zero.

   How to choose

Ask what the money is for.

  Preserving capital and passing it on?   A market where you own the asset outright.

  Producing income over a defined period you are comfortable with?   Bali is competitive and the demand is not in question.

  Both?   They are rarely the same asset, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling one of them.

   The comparison that actually matters

    Bali

t: Why is the Bali yield you were quoted wrong?
s: Because it is gross. Here is every deduction between the advertised figure and your bank account.
b:
An advertised Bali yield is almost always   gross  : annual revenue divided by purchase price. It is not wrong arithmetic. It is just not a return.

Here is the full distance between that number and what you keep.

   The deductions, in order

  Platform commission: 15–20%.   Airbnb, Booking.com and the rest take theirs before anything reaches you.

  PB1: 10%.   The regional accommodation tax, collected from the guest and remitted by the operator. Frequently presented as revenue in projections. It has never been yours.

  Management: 15–25%.   Charged on gross or on net after commission, depending on the contract. The difference is thousands a year.

  Running costs.   Staff, utilities, pool, garden, maintenance, supplies. A fixed monthly base that [does not fall when the villa is empty](/rental/bali villa running costs/).

  Refurbishment reserve: around 5%.   A rental villa needs refitting every few years. If it is not in the projection, it is coming out of your pocket instead.

  Income tax.   On whatever profit survives the above.

  Lease amortisation.   On a time limited right, the premium divided by the years remaining. Not a cash cost, an economic one, and the largest single item on a short lease.

   What that does to a headline

On a USD 300,000 leasehold villa at USD 180 a night and 65% occupancy:

     
             
  Advertised gross yield     12.0%    
  After costs and tax     1.9%    
  After lease amortisation, 25 years remaining     −2.1%    

Same property. Same revenue. Three very different numbers, and only one of them describes what happens to your money.

Ask four questions:

1.   Is this gross or net?   If they say net, ask which deductions are included, most "net" figures still omit refurbishment and amortisation.
2.   What occupancy does it assume, across the full year?

t: How does a spouse or family KITAS work?
s: Five different sub-indices depending on exactly who you are joining. Choosing the wrong one is the usual delay.
b:
"Spouse KITAS" is not one thing. The E31 family has five sub indices, and which one applies depends on   who   you are joining and   what status they hold  .

  Index   Relationship  
             
   E31A    Spouse of an Indonesian citizen (WNI)  
   E31B    Spouse of a principal ITAS/ITAP holder  
   E31E    Child of an ITAS/ITAP holder  
   E31H    Parent joining a principal permit holder  
   E31J    Child joining a sibling who holds ITAS/ITAP  

Applying as generic "spouse KITAS" without identifying the correct index is a common source of delay.

   What you need

For   E31A  , the marriage certificate must be registered with Indonesian Dukcapil, or, if you married abroad, legalised and translated, and properly reported to the relevant Indonesian authority.

That reporting step is the one people miss. An overseas marriage that was never reported is frequently the reason a file stalls, and fixing it afterwards takes longer than doing it in order.

For   E31B, E31E, E31H and E31J  , the principal must hold a valid, active ITAS or ITAP. Your permit is derivative of theirs, if theirs lapses, yours does not survive on its own.

You will also need proof of the specific relationship (birth certificates, translated and legalised where required) and minimum living funds evidence, commonly cited around   USD 2,000   equivalent.

   Duration

  E31A   runs one or two years. The others generally follow the sponsor's permit length, which can be 1, 2, 5 or 10 years depending on what the principal holds.

Renewable while the relationship and the sponsor's status remain valid.

   The permanent residence route

E31A leads to ITAP after   two consecutive years   of valid marriage based ITAS. It is the shortest ordinary route to permanent residence in Indonesia.

t: How safe is your money in a Bali property deal?
s: Safer than the horror stories suggest, and only if you do four specific things.
b:
People arrive here having read a horror story and assume the whole market is a trap. It is not. But the protections that exist in your home country mostly do not exist here, and the ones that do have to be arranged deliberately.

   The four things that actually protect you

  1. Your own notary.   Not the seller's, not the agent's, not the developer's. This is the single highest value protection available and the one most commonly skipped because the seller's notary is already there and seems easier.

  2. Verification at the land office.   The certificate is checked at the source. Photographs and photocopies mean nothing. Second certificates over the same parcel exist. So do sellers who are not the owner.

  3. A written refund trigger.   Before the deposit moves, in the agreement: what fails, who returns it, from which account, by when.

  4. Payment by bank transfer, never cash.   Traceable, dated, provable.

Do those four and most of what goes wrong here cannot happen to you.

   Where money actually disappears

  Nominee arrangements.   The land goes in an Indonesian person's name for you. Void since 1960, and since Perda Bali 4/2026 a criminal matter with liability extending to whoever facilitated it. You have no enforceable claim on something the law says never existed.

  Deposits with no refund mechanism.   Paid to hold a property, with nothing in writing about what happens if the checks fail.

  Off plan against a company that owns nothing.   If your only protection is a contract with an entity holding no assets, that is the risk in one sentence.

  Permits that were always coming.   Not a status. Ask for the application number.

   What the law will and will not do for you

It will enforce a genuine, properly documented lease. It will recognise a registered right held correctly.

It will not rescue an arrangement designed to work around the rules. There is no version where a court helps you enforce a structure the statute voids.

t: What is it really like to build a villa in Bali?
s: The permit sequence, the timeline by regency, and the parts of the process people do not budget for.
b:
Building here is genuinely rewarding and consistently slower than people plan for. Not because of construction. Because of everything before it.

   The order

  Spatial confirmation first.   Before design, before anything, confirm what the parcel permits. This is the gate. Everything downstream depends on it and it is the step people skip because it feels administrative.

  Then design to the constraints,   not to the view. Building coefficients cap your footprint and your total floor area. Setbacks come off before either applies. A beautiful design that ignores them gets redrawn.

  Then the building approval.   Submitted through the national system, verified administratively, then technically.

  Then build.   Then the certificate of functionality, which is what makes the finished building legally usable.

   Realistic timelines, from empty land to approval

  Regency   Time to approval  
             
  Denpasar   3 to 5 months  
  Gianyar   4 to 5 months  
  Tabanan   4 to 5 months  
  Badung   5 to 6 months  
  Klungkung   5 to 6 months  

Badung is where most people build and the slowest to approve, because volume creates the queue.

Add construction on top of that. Then the functionality certificate after.

   What people do not budget for

  Time.   Six months of approvals before a shovel moves is normal, not a delay.

  Resubmission.   Most of the delay in those figures is documents going back for deficiencies, not government processing. Complete files move.

  The environmental document,   at the level your project size requires.

  Neighbour consent,   which is a real step and occasionally a real negotiation.

  Site access for materials.   A plot down a narrow lane costs more to build on than the same plot on a road, and nobody prices this at purchase.

   The mistake that costs the most

Buying the land before confirming what it permits. It is the single most expensive error in this market, and it is entirely avoidable in about two weeks of checking.

t: Is Tabanan the next Canggu?
s: The clearest appreciation story in Bali and the hardest place to get a commercial accommodation project approved.
b:
Tabanan land runs 30–50% below Canggu, and the appreciation case is the most concrete in Bali: the Gilimanuk–Mengwi toll road, targeted for 2027–28, would cut the west coast drive from over three hours to roughly one.

That is the pitch. Here is what the pitch leaves out.

   Tabanan sits inside the moratorium

Tabanan is one of the six regencies covered by the construction moratorium. Zoning and permit diligence here is not a box to tick after signing. It determines whether the project exists at all.

   Tabanan is the most restrictive regency for commercial accommodation

Of the main investment regencies, Tabanan is generally the least permissive for short term accommodation. A plot that would support a rental villa in Badung may support only a private residence here.

Two constraints dominate:

    LP2B  , protected agricultural land, applied heavily across Tabanan, restricting conversion
    Coastal setbacks  , the most common single reason west coast deals collapse

The Tanah Lot corridor and Kedungu are exactly where both apply.

  Situation   Timeline  
             
  PBG from empty land   4–5 months  
  PBG + SLF for existing building   9–11 months  

Those timelines assume the project is permissible. Where LP2B or a setback blocks it, there is no timeline.

   The honest framing

Tabanan is a land appreciation play with an infrastructure catalyst. That can be a perfectly good investment.

It is a much weaker short term rental play today, and projections that apply Canggu occupancy and Canggu nightly rates to Tabanan land are describing a business that cannot currently be licensed on most of these plots.

  If someone is selling you Tabanan on rental yield rather than on appreciation, ask which business classification they intend to license, and in which zone.

   What to check

  Whether LP2B applies to the parcel. This is the first question, not the last
  Coastal setback, measured and confirmed in writing
  The RDTR designation and whether commercial acc

t: How much does it cost to rent in Bali?
s: One-bedroom villas start around IDR 17.5 million a month in Canggu. The bigger shock is that most landlords want a year up front.
b:
Almost everyone rents here before they buy, and the rental market tells you more about an area than any listing site will.

   What renting in Bali actually costs

  One bedroom villas   start from around   IDR 17,500,000 a month in Canggu  , and around   IDR 15,600,000 in Seminyak  .

  Two bedroom villas   run roughly   IDR 15 to 45 million a month  . That spread is not a mistake. Location, pool, condition, furnishing and how well you negotiate all move it substantially.

Within Canggu,   Berawa and Batu Bolong   carry a premium over nearly everywhere else. Central Ubud is not the bargain people expect, though prices drop quickly on the outskirts.   Sanur is consistently cheaper   than Canggu for equivalent space, which is one of the reasons families cluster there.

   The thing nobody warns you about

  Annual contracts are usually paid in full, up front.  

This is the single biggest gap between the budget people plan and the reality they meet. You do not pay monthly as you would at home. A landlord quoting an attractive annual rate commonly wants all twelve months in one transfer before handing over keys.

Monthly rentals exist and are far more flexible, but you pay a real premium for that flexibility. Most long term listings want a   minimum of one to three months  , and many want six or twelve paid at once.

For anything beyond six months, an annual contract is normally better value if you can fund it.

  Payment   Rolling   Usually full amount up front  
  Flexibility   High   Low  
  Best for   First three months, testing an area   Anyone staying six months or more  

The sensible pattern is monthly for your first stretch while you work out where you actually want to be, then annual once you know.

    Is electricity included?   Usually not. Air conditioning across several bedrooms is a genuine monthly cost.

t: Apartment or villa: which returns more in Bali?
s: Apartments carry lower running costs and a licensing route that villas lost in 2026. Villas carry the higher rate.
b:
The comparison is usually made on nightly rate, which is the least important variable.

    Villa   Apartment  
                   
  Nightly rate   Higher   Lower  
  Occupancy   More seasonal   Steadier  
  Running costs   High: staff, pool, garden   Lower, often shared  
  Entry price   Higher   Lower  
  Break even occupancy   Higher   Lower  
  Licensing route for a new foreign owned company     Closed   for villa classification   Apartment hotel remains open  
  Exit liquidity   Deeper buyer pool   Narrower in most Bali locations

Since 22 July 2026, the   villa classification (55203) is closed to new PT PMA registration   in Bali.   Apartment hotel (55204) remains open, at any size.  

That is not a small administrative distinction. For a foreign investor forming a new company to operate nightly rentals, it changes which asset types have a lawful operating route at all. [The detail is here](/company/pt pma kbli closure bali/).

A villa carries its own staff, pool and garden. An apartment usually shares building costs across units, which lowers the fixed base, and the fixed base is what sets [break even occupancy](/rental/bali villa break even occupancy/).

Lower fixed costs mean a lower break even, which means more tolerance for a bad season. That resilience rarely appears in a comparison built on nightly rate.

Rate and demand. A well located, well run villa with a pool commands a premium an apartment cannot, and Bali's guest expectation is villa shaped.

For a buyer who will use the property personally, that matters beyond the numbers.

Run both through the [calculator](/calculator/) with realistic figures for each. The property type selector adjusts the cost assumptions. Compare   net yield after amortisation   and   break even occupancy  , not headline rates.

t: Where does a Bali villa get its water?
s: Piped supply does not reach everywhere, wells need permits, and on the Bukit water is a genuine operating cost rather than a detail.
b:
This is the diligence item most often skipped and most expensive to discover afterwards.

   The three sources

  PDAM  , the municipal piped supply. Reliable where it exists, cheap, and it does not reach everywhere. Coverage is patchy outside the main settled areas and pressure varies.

  A bore well.   Common on larger plots. Groundwater extraction is regulated and requires permits, and depth and yield vary enormously by geology.

  Trucked water.   Delivered by tanker into a storage tank. This is the fallback where the first two are unavailable or insufficient, and it is a real, recurring operating cost.

Many villas run a combination: piped supply where available, a well for the garden and pool, and a tanker in dry season when the others fall short.

   Why the Bukit is different

The Bukit peninsula is limestone: porous, elevated and historically thin on accessible groundwater. Properties there frequently rely on trucked water, and in a dry year the cost and availability both move against you.

If you are buying on the Bukit, ask specifically how the property is supplied, what it costs per month with the villa full in dry season, and what happens in a bad year. It is the question sellers there are least prepared for and the one that most affects your operating budget.

  Is there a PDAM connection, and is it active?
  If there is a well, does it hold the required permits?
  What is the well's yield, and has it been tested in dry season?
  Where is the storage tank and what is its capacity?
  What did the property spend on water in the last twelve months?
  Is there a filtration system, and when was it last serviced?

Ask for actual bills or delivery invoices rather than an estimate. A seller who cannot produce twelve months of water cost is telling you something.

Even on piped supply, a villa needs storage. Pressure drops, supply interrupts, and a pool plus guests plus laundry is a demanding load.

t: Is Lombok a better bet than Bali right now?
s: Cheaper land, and, crucially, Bali's 2026 restrictions do not apply there. Different province, different rules.
b:
Lombok gets recommended as "Bali twenty years ago", which is a slogan rather than an analysis. The substantive argument is different, and stronger.

   The point almost nobody makes

  Lombok is not in Bali province.   It is in West Nusa Tenggara (NTB).

That distinction is not geographic trivia. It determines which rules apply.

    Bali   Lombok (NTB)  
                   
  National land law: UUPA 5/1960, PP 18/2021   Applies     Applies identically    
  Bali's 18 closed business classifications (22 July 2026)   Applies     Does not apply    
  Perda Bali 4/2026 on nominee arrangements   Applies     Does not apply    
  Spatial planning and RDTR   Bali regencies   NTB regencies, different rules  

So the villa and homestay classifications [closed to new foreign owned companies in Bali](/company/pt pma kbli closure bali/) are a   Bali provincial measure  . A project in Lombok is assessed under NTB rules.

For an investor whose Bali structure stopped working in July 2026, that is a material difference, and it is the actual reason to look at Lombok, rather than the price.

   What does not change

  Foreigners still cannot own freehold anywhere in Indonesia.   UUPA 5/1960 is national law. The same three routes apply: leasehold, Hak Pakai with residency, or HGB through a PT PMA.

  Nominee arrangements are still void nationally.   Perda Bali 4/2026 added criminal exposure and facilitator liability in Bali specifically, but the underlying arrangement has been void under Article 26(2) since 1960, everywhere. Lombok is not a workaround.

  Every land right except Hak Milik still expires.  

   What is genuinely different

  Mandalika   is a national special economic zone on the south coast, with the MotoGP circuit as its anchor, state backed development rather than organic growth.

  Land is materially cheaper  , and the tourism base is far smaller. That is both the opportunity and the risk.

t: How much should you actually pay for a Bali villa?
s: Work backwards from the return you need. The price that makes a deal work is often well below the asking price.
b:
Most buyers start from the asking price and ask whether the yield is acceptable. Reverse it: start from the return you require and calculate what price delivers it.

That number is your ceiling. Everything above it is someone else's margin.

   The method

  1. Establish realistic revenue.   Achievable nightly rate at honest full year occupancy. Not the seller's figure, the area's.

  2. Subtract every cost.   Platform commission, the 10% regional tax, management, staff and running costs, refurbishment reserve, income tax.

  3. Decide the return you need.   For an illiquid foreign asset with legal and currency risk, wanting 8–10% net is not greedy. It is priced for the risk you are taking.

  4. Divide.   Net profit ÷ required return = the maximum total capital that works.

  5. Subtract everything that is not the purchase price.   Transaction costs around 7%, furniture and setup, any build or renovation. What remains is the most you can pay.

The [calculator](/calculator/) does steps 1 to 4, adjust the price until the net yield reaches your number.

   On a lease, add the step everyone skips

A leasehold consumes its premium. To compare it honestly against a freehold, either:

  Require a   higher   net yield to compensate for the asset ending, or
  Use the   return after amortisation   as your decision figure

  An operator classification that lawfully covers nightly rental

t: Is Bali safe?
s: Violent crime is not the risk. The roads are, by a wide margin, and almost nobody prepares for that.
b:
Yes, broadly. Bali is not a dangerous place by international standards, and violent crime against foreigners is rare.

But the honest answer is that the actual risks here are not the ones people ask about.

   The real risk is the road

This is the one that hurts people, and it is not close.

Bali runs on scooters. Traffic is dense, lane discipline is loose, and a lot of foreigners ride for the first time in their lives here, on unfamiliar roads, often without a proper licence, sometimes in flip flops.

Wet season makes it worse. Roads flood, visibility drops, and the surface gets genuinely slippery.

  If you do one thing for your safety here, it is this.   Wear a real helmet. Do not ride at night on unlit roads if you can avoid it. And check whether your travel insurance actually covers scooter accidents, because a great many policies exclude them unless you hold the correct licence.

That last point catches people constantly. An excluded claim after a serious accident is how a holiday becomes a financial disaster.

   Petty theft

Bag snatching from scooters happens, particularly in busier areas at night. Phone snatching too.

It is opportunistic rather than violent. Do not hang a bag off your handlebars, do not walk with your phone out at the roadside, and it mostly stops being an issue.

   Health

Dengue is present. Use repellent, especially around dusk, and take standing water around a rental seriously.

Stomach problems are common in the first weeks while you adjust. Unpleasant, rarely serious.

The thing to plan for is   serious illness or injury  , because that is where costs escalate fast. [Healthcare, hospitals and what insurance actually needs to cover is here](/living/healthcare in bali/).

   Natural events

Bali sits in a seismically active region. Earthquakes and volcanic activity are real but infrequent. It is not something to organise your life around, but it belongs in a construction and insurance conversation if you are building.

t: Which visa lets you come and check out a property properly?
s: There is a purpose-built pre-investment category. Most buyers use a tourist visa and run out of time.
b:
Most people looking at Bali property arrive on a visa on arrival, spend thirty days trying to do due diligence properly, extend once, and leave with the work half done.

There is a category built for exactly this, and almost nobody uses it.

   The pre investment visas

  Index   Type   Duration  
                   
   C12    Single entry pre investment   Commonly around 60 days, extendable  
   D12    Multiple entry pre investment     180 days, extendable by a further 180: up to 12 months total    

 D12  is the useful one. Multiple entry, six months at a time, up to a year in total. It is designed for site visits, due diligence, and meetings with counsel and agents before committing to an investment.

For anyone seriously evaluating a purchase, walking plots, verifying certificates at BPN, sitting with a notary, checking zoning at the regency office. That is the difference between doing it properly and doing it in a rush.

   What it does not authorise

Neither C12 nor D12 permits:

  Signing on as an employee
  Running a business day to day
  Drawing Indonesian income

They are visitor categories. Once the investment is actually made, you move to the relevant [E28 investor route](/visas/investor kitas e28a/).

   Why this matters for the due diligence itself

The checks that actually protect you take time, and several cannot be rushed:

  Certificate verification at the local BPN office through your own notary
  Zoning and RDTR confirmation at the regency planning office
  Confirming KDB and KLB for the specific parcel
  Establishing every setback in writing
  Confirming PBG and SLF status for anything already built
  Verifying the operator's NIB and business classification

Two to four weeks is a realistic minimum for thorough due diligence, and that assumes offices respond promptly. A thirty day tourist visa with a flight home at the end of it produces exactly the pressure that makes people skip steps.

t: What should you know about buying on Nusa Penida?
s: Bali's rules apply in full, permits take longest of any regency, and infrastructure is the constraint nobody prices.
b:
Nusa Penida is sold as the frontier, dramatic coastline, visitor numbers climbing, land at a fraction of the Bukit.

Before the price, one fact does most of the work.

   It is Klungkung, and Klungkung is Bali

Nusa Penida sits in   Klungkung regency, Bali province  . Everything that applies on the mainland applies here in full:

  [The 18 business classifications closed to new foreign owned companies](/company/pt pma kbli closure bali/) in July 2026
  Perda Bali 4/2026 on nominee arrangements, including facilitator liability
  Bali provincial spatial policy

Unlike [Lombok](/areas/lombok property foreigners/), this is not a different regulatory environment. It is the same one, administered by a smaller office.

   Permits take longest here

Klungkung is the slowest regency in Bali for building approvals:

    Klungkung   Denpasar, for comparison  
                   
  PBG from empty land     5–6 months     3–5 months  
  PBG + SLF for an existing building     10–12 months     8–10 months  

The reasons are structural rather than temporary: a smaller technical team, longer queues for evaluation and inspection, and, specific to the Nusas,   marine and spatial coordination   that mainland projects do not trigger.

Coastal and cliff edge sites, which is most of what gets marketed here, are precisely the ones that attract that additional review.

   The constraint that decides projects

Infrastructure, and it is not a permitting question.

  Water   is the binding limit on Nusa Penida. Supply is genuinely scarce, and a villa with a pool and guest turnover is a heavy consumer. Establish the actual water source and its reliability across a dry season before anything else. This is the constraint most likely to make an otherwise sound project unworkable.

t: Why did all the Indonesian visa codes change?
s: The system went from 133 indices to 110 in 2025, and employer-sponsored work visas from 31 to 6. Old advice is now wrong.
b:
If you are reading a blog post, a forum thread, or an agent's brochure written before mid 2025, the visa codes in it are probably wrong.

The Directorate General of Immigration restructured the classification system in 2025 under   Decree M.IP 08.GR.01.01/2025  :

  Total indices reduced from   133 to 110  
  Employer sponsored work visa types cut from   31 to 6  
  Twenty former sector specific corporate work codes (E23B–E23W) unified into a single   E23   index

Then in January 2026, GCI was launched on top of it.

   The rule underneath the whole system

This is the part that survives every reshuffle:

  Do not choose a visa based on how long you want to stay. The first legal question is always what you will   actually do   in Indonesia.

Work, investment, family, study, medical treatment, remote employment, ancestry, or simply visiting. The activity determines the index, the sponsor requirement and the legal basis. Length of stay falls out of that answer. It is not the input.

Using a visitor status for unauthorised work is an enforcement risk, not a technicality.

   E34    Medical treatment  
   E35    Reciprocal work and holiday

    What it is

    ITAP     Permanent stay, converted

t: Should you renovate a villa in Bali?
s: Older stock is cheap for a reason. Renovation can be the best value in the market or a way to buy someone else's permit problem.
b:
A large share of the villa stock in Seminyak, Canggu and Sanur is ten to twenty years old, and tropical wear is fast. Renovation is therefore a real strategy here rather than an edge case.

   Why it can work

Buying tired stock in a proven location, at a discount that exceeds the cost of putting it right, is one of the few reliable value plays left in the developed corridors where land is scarce.

You are buying the location and the land, which is the part that holds value, and replacing the part that depreciates.

   The permit trap

This is where renovations go wrong.

Structural change requires PBG approval, and completion requires SLF. If the existing building has neither, or if extensions were built outside the original approval, you are not renovating a compliant building. You are inheriting a compliance problem and adding to it.

Before you buy, establish:

  Do PBG and SLF exist, and do they describe the building as it currently stands?
  Were extensions, staff quarters, additional structures or converted spaces approved?
  Does the building fit inside current KDB, KLB, height limits and setbacks?
  Is there a verified, costed path to regularising anything that does not?

A building inside a setback or breaching the coverage limit cannot be regularised at any price. Documentation gaps usually can. The difference decides whether the project is a bargain or a trap.

   What renovation actually costs

Full renovation frequently lands close to new build cost per square metre, because you pay to remove before you pay to build, and you work around an existing structure rather than to a clean design.

Budget separately for:

  Demolition and disposal   Underestimated, and slower than expected  
  Structural repair   Damp, termites, corroded reinforcement  
  Rewiring and replumbing   Usually necessary on older stock  
  Pool resurfacing and plant   Frequently overdue

t: Is Bali property a bubble?
s: Prices have run hard. Whether that is a bubble depends on which part of the market you are looking at.
b:
Fair question, and the honest answer is that Bali is two markets right now and only one of them looks stretched.

   What is not a bubble

Demand is real and measurable. Nearly   7 million foreign arrivals in 2025  , up almost 10% year on year. Australia alone accounts for 1.63 million. The airport is expanding from roughly 24 to 32 million passengers.

Luxury operators have committed. Bulgari, Six Senses and Alila do not guess.

And supply of the thing that actually matters is capped. Not land, which exists, but   properly zoned, permitted, licensable land  , which is a fraction of the island and is getting harder to add to rather than easier.

That is not the shape of a bubble. That is scarcity meeting demand.

   What does look stretched

The oversupply is in one specific thing:   small villas in Canggu marketed on rental yield.  

Everyone built the same product for the same guest. Nightly rates in that segment are being squeezed by the volume of near identical options, while land prices kept climbing on the assumption that rates would not soften.

When the advertised yield stops arriving, the price paid for the land stops making sense. That is the part to be careful with.

  Pink zoned, fully permitted assets   Unpermitted villas sold at a discount  
  Long remaining terms   Short leases priced like long ones  
  Areas with capped supply   Canggu small villa rental stock  
  Land bought as land   Land bought on a yield projection  

   The thing that changed in 2026

Bali closed several accommodation classifications to new foreign owned companies in July. That does two things at once: it makes it harder to add new licensed rental supply, and it makes   existing properly licensed assets more valuable  .

Policy is tightening, not loosening. That supports the compliant end of the market and squeezes the informal end.

t: What is healthcare in Bali actually like?
s: Routine care is fine and affordable. Serious care is where people get financially destroyed, and the number is bigger than you think.
b:
Routine healthcare in Bali is better than most people expect and cheap by Western standards. Serious healthcare is where the real financial exposure sits, and it is the thing almost nobody plans for properly.

   The hospitals foreigners use

  BIMC  , in Nusa Dua and Kuta. International standard, priced accordingly. BIMC Nusa Dua was named Medical Tourism Hospital of the Year for Indonesia at the Healthcare Asia Awards 2025.

  Siloam  , several locations. The common choice for expat families who want good care without BIMC pricing.

  Bali International Hospital  , opened in 2024 inside the Sanur special economic zone. This is the most significant change to healthcare here in years. It was built specifically so that complex cases would not all have to fly to Singapore or Australia.

English is spoken at all three.

   What things cost

    Typical cost  
             
  Consultation   USD 40 to 100  
  Emergency room visit   USD 150 to 300  
  Standard room, per night   USD 300 to 500  
  ICU, per night   USD 1,500 to 2,500  
  Minor surgery   USD 500 to 2,000  

Without insurance, a standard emergency case runs   USD 5,000 to 25,000  .

   The number that actually matters

  Medical evacuation to Singapore costs USD 55,000 to 100,000.  

That is the figure that determines whether an accident is a bad week or a life altering financial event. If local care cannot handle your case, that flight is the difference, and nobody has that sitting in a current account.

   What your insurance actually needs

  At least USD 100,000 to 250,000 of medical evacuation cover.   Not general medical cover. Evacuation specifically, named in the policy.

  Direct billing agreements with Bali hospitals.   Without this you pay up front and claim it back later, and private hospitals here will ask for payment or a deposit before treating a serious case. Being right about your entitlement does not help you at 2am.

t: What do villa staff cost in Bali?
s: Base salaries are low. The employer obligations on top of them, BPJS and the mandatory annual bonus, are what owners forget to budget.
b:
Staff are usually the single largest fixed cost of running a villa here, and they are owed whether or not a guest ever arrives.

   Monthly base salaries

  Role   Monthly, USD  
             
  Housekeeper   120 to 300  
  Gardener   50 to 120  
  Pool service   30 to 70  
  Security   120 to 200  
  Villa manager   300 to 600  
  Cook   150 to 350  

A typical three bedroom villa runs two to three staff, roughly IDR 7M to 12M a month in base salaries combined.

   The costs on top of base salary

This is where owners get caught out, because these are legal obligations rather than optional extras.

  BPJS contributions.   Employer contributions to the national health and employment social security schemes add roughly 14 percent on top of salary. This is not discretionary for properly employed staff.

  THR.   Tunjangan Hari Raya is the mandatory religious holiday allowance: one full month of salary, paid annually before the holiday. Every employee with twelve months of service is entitled to it, and pro rata below that.

So a team costing IDR 7M a month in base salary is not costing IDR 84M a year. Add BPJS and THR and the real annual figure for a two person team lands closer to   IDR 84M to 100M  .

   Regional minimum wage

Bali sets a provincial minimum wage annually, and regencies set their own within it. Badung, which covers Canggu, Seminyak and the airport side, runs the highest in the province. Paying below the applicable minimum is a labour law problem, not a negotiation.

   Employed or contracted?

Owners sometimes prefer to treat staff as contractors to avoid BPJS and THR. Whether that holds depends on the substance of the relationship, not the label on the paperwork: fixed hours, a single employer, direction and control all point to employment.

Getting this wrong is a labour dispute, and Indonesian labour law is protective of workers. Take local advice rather than assuming the arrangement you prefer is the one that applies.

t: What does it cost to furnish a villa in Bali?
s: Furniture is cheap and good here. What owners get wrong is how fast it wears out and how rarely it is included in a build quote.
b:
Fit out is almost never inside the per square metre construction rate, and it is a substantial line on its own.

   Why buying locally is the right call

Bali has a genuine furniture industry. Teak, suar wood, rattan, terrazzo, upholstery and custom joinery are made here at prices well below Europe, Australia or North America, and the styles suit the climate and the guest expectation.

The workshops around Gianyar and along the Denpasar corridor will build to drawing. Custom is normal rather than a luxury, and the lead times are weeks rather than months.

For a three bedroom villa, furnishing to a standard that competes in the nightly rental market:

  Level   Total, USD  
             
  Basic, functional   15,000 to 25,000  
  Good rental standard   25,000 to 45,000  
  High specification   50,000 and up

Guests judge on photographs. Under furnishing to save USD 10,000 on a property costing hundreds of thousands is a false economy that shows up directly in the nightly rate.

t: Can you retire in Bali, and what does it take?
s: There is a route built for it. The requirements are financial rather than age-based, and property gives you nothing.
b:
Yes, and the route is more straightforward than most people expect. It is also not the one most people are told about.

   The route

The   Second Home   family covers financially independent residence with no employer, no business and no family sponsor. The standard tier is commonly cited at either a deposit of around   USD 130,000   in an Indonesian state bank, or qualifying property of around   USD 1,000,000  .

Verify both at the point of filing. These thresholds get revised.

What you get is   five or ten years  , which is what makes it attractive against a permit you renew annually.

   The senior tiers people miss

Within that same family there are dedicated senior or elderly tiers, commonly cited at a minimum age of 55 or 60 depending on the sub index, with income, pension or deposit conditions instead of the full standard threshold.

If you are over 55, ask about these specifically before defaulting to the standard tier. Agents frequently do not mention them.

   The thing that catches people

  Buying a villa does not let you stay.   Property and immigration are unrelated systems in Indonesia. You can own a house here and have no right to be in it beyond a tourist stay.

That surprises people constantly, and it is the most expensive misunderstanding in this market.

   What to think about beyond the visa

  Healthcare.   Routine care locally is fine. Serious care usually means Singapore. Comprehensive international insurance, and check the age limits on the policy before you commit to the move.

  Tax.   Presence, not passport. Beyond 183 days you are an Indonesian tax resident. That has consequences for pension income depending on your home country's treaty position, and it is a conversation to have before you arrive.

  The deposit is not a fee.   Confirm whether it must be maintained continuously, and in what account type, before you move the money.

t: What do international schools in Bali cost?
s: From around USD 3,000 to over USD 30,000 a year. And the headline tuition is not the number you actually pay.
b:
For most families, school fees are the single largest line in a Bali budget. Larger than rent, frequently by a wide margin.

   The range

Annual tuition runs from around   USD 3,000   at early years bilingual centres to   over USD 30,000   at premium campuses.

The established international schools sit at roughly   USD 15,000 to 28,000 per student per year  , depending on grade level.

  Green School Bali  , in Ubud, runs approximately   USD 18,000 to 27,000+   a year depending on grade.

  Canggu Community School   runs from roughly   IDR 110 million   for Early Years to   IDR 257 million   for the IB Diploma years.

Headline tuition is not what you pay. Once everything is added:

    Annual  
             
  Registration   USD 500 to 2,500  
  Uniforms   USD 150 to 400  
  Transport   USD 1,200 to 3,600  
  Lunch   USD 600 to 1,200  

  All in, budget USD 8,000 to 28,000 per child per year  , depending on school and grade.

For two children at an established school, that is a serious annual commitment before you have paid rent, and it is why family budgets here land in a completely different bracket to single or couple budgets.

  Ubud   is home to the schools known internationally for creativity and sustainability, Green School most famously.

t: Can you legally work remotely from Bali?
s: Yes, and there is a specific permit for it. Most people arrive on the wrong one.
b:
Yes, legally, on a defined route. The problem is that most people work here on a tourist status, which is not a grey area.

   The right permit

  E33G   covers a foreign national who stays employed by, or contracted to, a company established outside Indonesia, and wants residence here without becoming locally employed.

The published criteria are specific:

  A genuine employment or consulting agreement with a   foreign   company
  Minimum annual income commonly cited at   USD 60,000  
  General living funds, commonly cited around USD 2,000
    No income from Indonesian entities at all  

It runs one year and renews while the arrangement and the income continue.

   What it does not cover

It is not a general freelancer permit. If you cannot document both the foreign employment relationship and the income level, you likely do not qualify, whatever an agent tells you.

It also does not permit any Indonesian sourced income. Take on a local client and you are outside the terms.

   The mistake almost everyone makes

Working on a visitor status. A visa on arrival gives 30 days plus one extension. It permits tourism and meetings. It does not permit work, and the fact that your employer is abroad does not change that.

This is enforced. It is not a technicality.

   The part nobody plans for

  Tax residence follows presence, not your visa.   Past 183 days in a year you are an Indonesian tax resident, even though every dollar you earn is foreign.

This is the single most misunderstood point among remote workers here, and it is worth a conversation with a tax adviser before you cross that line rather than after.

Buying does not give you the right to stay, and the E33G is not framed as a route to permanent residence. If long term security is the goal, [look at the routes that do lead there](/visas/kitap itap indonesia/) before you commit capital.

t: Is Seminyak still worth buying in?
s: The most established foreign market on the island. Highest density, highest prices, almost no land, and the deepest resale pool.
b:
Seminyak is what Canggu is becoming. It was the expatriate and tourism centre before Canggu had a paved road, and it is now effectively built out.

s: Listing a villa nightly is a licensed commercial activity. Plenty of listings do not hold that licence, and enforcement has tightened.
b:

  The building   PBG approval and SLF certificate

  The classification   Valid, current, and matching how the property actually operates

Missing any layer and the listing is exposed regardless of how many years it has run without trouble.

On 22 July 2026 Bali closed a set of low risk classifications to new foreign owned company registration, including villa and homestay. t: Is solar worth it for a Bali villa?
s: The sunshine is excellent and the electricity bill is large, which makes the arithmetic better here than in most places owners come from.
b:
Bali sits near the equator with strong, consistent irradiance year round. Combined with an electricity bill driven by air conditioning and pool plant, that makes solar genuinely worth modelling.

   Why the load profile suits it

Solar generates during the day. A villa's daytime load is exactly what solar is good at:

  Pool pump, which runs for hours every day
  Air conditioning, heaviest in the afternoon heat
  Water pumps and heating
  General household load

That daytime alignment is the reason the economics work better here than for a house whose consumption is mostly in the evening.

System cost scales with capacity. A villa system sized to cover a meaningful share of daytime load is a five figure investment in USD, with the exact number depending on panels, inverter, roof suitability and whether you add batteries.

Batteries roughly double the cost and are what let you ride through outages. Without them, a grid tied system stops when the grid does, which surprises owners who bought solar partly for resilience.

Given that short outages are routine here, the resilience argument is worth weighing rather than dismissing.

Whether and how you are credited for exported power is set by regulation and has changed. Do not size a system on the assumption that generous export credit exists.

The safer design is one that covers your own daytime consumption well rather than one built to export surplus. Confirm the current rules before committing.

s: The internet is better than the reputation. The legal position is worse than most people assume.
b:
Two separate questions get mixed together here. Can you physically work from Bali, and can you legally work from Bali. The answers are different.

   The infrastructure is fine now

  Fibre connections of 50 to 100 Mbps are standard   in the main expat areas. That is a genuine change from a few years ago, when the answer to this question was much less encouraging.

For calls, screen sharing and normal remote work, it is not a limitation.

What still catches people:

    Power cuts happen.   Usually short. A laptop with battery is fine, a desktop is not.
    Villa internet varies wildly.   The villa's connection is not the area's connection. Test it before you sign anything longer than a month.
    Get a local SIM immediately   with a decent data package. It is cheap and it is your backup when the villa connection drops mid call.
    Time zones.   Excellent for Asia and Australia. Workable for Europe with early starts. Genuinely hard for the US.

   The legal position

This is where it matters, and it changed this year.

In   April 2026   Indonesian immigration launched a dedicated Bali patrol task force. In its first three weeks it   detained 62 foreign nationals   for illegal work, overstays and document violations. Officers patrol Canggu, Ubud, Seminyak, Kerobokan and Uluwatu, and they check public social media and LinkedIn.

Working on a tourist visa is not a grey area and is being enforced. [The detail is here](/visas/bali visa crackdown 2026/).

   The permit that covers it

  E33G   exists specifically for people employed by or contracted to a company outside Indonesia. The published criteria are specific:

  A genuine foreign employment or consulting agreement
  Minimum annual income commonly cited at   USD 60,000  
  No income from Indonesian entities at all

It runs a year and renews while both conditions hold. [Full requirements here](/visas/digital nomad bali/).

t: Do you need a prenup to own property in a mixed marriage?
s: Without one, a foreign spouse's interest can contaminate an Indonesian spouse's freehold. This is the most consequential document in a mixed marriage here.
b:
This is the single most important legal document for a foreigner married to an Indonesian citizen who intends to hold property, and it is routinely skipped.

   The problem

Under Indonesian marriage law, property acquired during a marriage is treated as joint marital property by default. Both spouses have an interest in it.

Hak Milik, Indonesian freehold, may only be held by an Indonesian citizen. Put those two rules together and the difficulty appears immediately: if an Indonesian spouse acquires freehold land during a marriage to a foreigner, the foreign spouse acquires an interest in a title a foreigner cannot lawfully hold.

The consequence is not theoretical. It can force disposal of the land, block the purchase at the notary stage, or surface years later on divorce, death or sale.

   What the agreement does

A prenuptial agreement separates the spouses' assets, so that property acquired by the Indonesian spouse is their own rather than joint. That removes the foreign interest and allows the Indonesian spouse to hold freehold normally.

It also protects the foreign spouse, by making clear what is theirs and what is not, which matters enormously if the marriage ends.

   If you are already married

Until 2015 the answer was that you were too late. The Constitutional Court decision in 69/PUU XIII/2015 changed that, and a   postnuptial   agreement separating assets is now possible.

It has to be properly executed before a notary and registered with the civil registry and, where relevant, noted so that it is discoverable. An unregistered agreement in a drawer does not do the job.

If you are already married, already here, and already own or intend to own land, this is the item to deal with before anything else.

   What it does not fix

A prenuptial agreement does not make a foreigner able to hold Hak Milik. Nothing does. It separates the estates so the Indonesian spouse can hold it cleanly in their own name.

t: What is the Bali property market doing in 2026?
s: Land in well-zoned coastal locations is holding. The standardised villa rental business built on it is where the pressure actually is.
b:
There are two markets here behaving differently, and most commentary confuses them.

   Land versus the business on it

  Land   in tourism zoned coastal locations is genuinely scarce. It cannot be manufactured, and it came through a complete tourism shutdown in 2020 and 2021 with prime locations intact. That scarcity is real and it supports price.

  The nightly rental villa business   depends on guest nights, achievable rates, licensing and competition. All four have moved against new entrants.

Calling the whole island overheated misses that the stress is concentrated in the second market.

   What is actually happening to supply

Construction of the standard three bedroom pool villa has run ahead of guest night growth in the main corridors. Pererenan and Cemagi in particular were rice fields in 2019 and are now dense with near identical product.

When two hundred functionally identical villas list in the same window, they compete on price, because nothing else separates them. That shows up first as softer nightly rates and higher vacancy, which is a yield problem before it is a valuation problem.

Differentiated property still performs. Generic property increasingly does not.

   The regulatory variable

In roughly one year: 18 business classifications closed to new foreign owned registration, facilitating nominee land arrangements criminalised, KBLI renumbered with a migration deadline, and a dedicated immigration task force deployed that detained 62 foreign nationals in its first three weeks.

Regulation moves faster here than the market cycle does, and it can strand a business model in a quarter. Anyone underwriting Bali purely on historical appreciation is watching the wrong variable.

The useful precedent already happened. Tourism stopped, income stopped, and a genuine distressed window opened where leaseholds and operating villas traded well below prior pricing.

t: Do you need a licence to drive a scooter in Bali?
s: Yes. And the reason it matters is not the police fine, it is what happens to your insurance claim.
b:
Almost everyone here gets around on a scooter. Most foreigners riding one are not properly licensed for it, and most of them have not thought through what that means.

   What you actually need

To ride legally you need either:

  An   International Driving Permit   endorsed for motorcycles, issued in your home country before you travel, alongside your home licence, or
  An   Indonesian licence (SIM)  , which you can apply for locally

The key detail is the   motorcycle endorsement  . A car licence plus an IDP that only covers cars does not make you legal on a scooter, and this is where most people are caught out without realising.

Rental shops will hand you a bike without checking any of this. That is not permission, it is just a shop that wants your money.

   Why it matters more than the fine

Police checks happen and the on the spot fine is an inconvenience.

  The real exposure is your insurance.  

A great many travel and health policies   exclude motorbike accidents unless you hold the correct licence   for the engine size you are riding. So the sequence that ruins people is:

1. Accident
2. Serious injury
3. Hospital, potentially evacuation
4. Claim denied because you were not properly licensed

Given that [medical evacuation to Singapore runs USD 55,000 to 100,000](/living/healthcare in bali/), that denied claim is not a paperwork problem. It is the most expensive consequence of a decision people make in about four seconds at a rental shop.

   Practical advice

  Get the endorsement before you fly.   Adding motorcycles to an IDP at home is cheap and quick. Doing it retrospectively is not possible.

  Wear a proper helmet  , not the token one the rental shop provides.

  Do not ride at night on unlit roads   if you can avoid it. Most of Bali outside the main strips has no street lighting.

  Rainy season changes everything.   Roads flood, drainage is inconsistent, and the surface goes slick within seconds of rain starting.
